# The Night Count

I kept the keys to the old mill for eleven winters. Every night I walked the yard with my cap pulled low and counted the windows on the north wall, nine of them, always nine.

The night the count came to ten, I stood under the extra window a long time. Then I took the ring of keys from my belt and tried every one in the door beneath it. None of them turned.

I walked back to the gatehouse and wrote the number in the book, and I have not been back to the north wall since.
